heroHeadline: Day 953: Former Hostages Liri Albag and Omri Miran Describe 'Closure' After al-Haddad Killing — While October Council Simultaneously Renews Demand for Independent Probe With 46 Days to Supreme Court's July 1 Deadline; Hamas Has No Named Military Successor
heroSubtitle: The deadliest attack on Jewish people since the Holocaust — assault timeline, hostage crisis resolved January 2026, intelligence failures, and IDF response. May 17, 2026 (Day 953): The day after the IDF confirmed the killing of Izz al-Din al-Haddad — head of Hamas's military wing and the last known senior architect of October 7 still in Gaza — former Israeli hostages who had been personally held by al-Haddad offered public reactions. Omri Miran (former captive, personally encountered al-Haddad in Gaza tunnels): 'Like a type of small victory, a victory over evil. He proudly boasted how he was an architect of the October 7 massacre.' Liri Albag (one of five Nahal Oz surveillance soldiers kidnapped by al-Haddad): 'Every dog gets its day, and you are a hell of a dog.' Emily Damari: 'He planned October 7, murdered my friends and many other dear people, and planned my kidnapping and held me in Hamas tunnels.' Simultaneously, the October Council and bereaved families renewed demands for an independent October 7 state commission — with 46 days to the Supreme Court's July 1 investigation deadline and the Kallner inquiry bill (which stripped 'independent investigation' language and bars judges) advancing toward a first plenum reading in late May. Hamas has not named a military successor; political bureau operating under five-member collective leadership. Accountability front: 46 days remain until July 1 — the High Court's deadline for the government to present a 'suitable' investigation framework. JPPI poll (May 15): 63% of Israelis support an independent commission. UN Security Council held an open debate on May 17 calling for consolidation of the October 2025 ceasefire and halt to Israeli violations: 2,400+ violations documented, 857+ Palestinians killed since ceasefire began October 10, 2025. Israel controls 60%+ of Gaza; reconstruction funding nearly absent (<$1B of $17B pledged received). Gaza ceasefire Phase Two remains deadlocked: Hamas refuses disarmament without political guarantees Israel will not provide. IDF operational plans for resumed offensive complete, pending US authorization.
footerNote: Data sourced from IDF, Israel Police, UN OCHA, Israeli government, Bloomberg, Reuters, AP, Haaretz, Times of Israel, Jerusalem Post, WAFA, and institutional analyses. Casualty figures are official Israeli counts; Hamas-theater figures are separately noted and contested. All 251 hostages accounted for as of January 26, 2026. Cumulative conflict dead (Oct 7, 2023 – May 17, 2026): 72,600+ Palestinians per OCHA/Gaza MoH/WAFA. Ceasefire in effect since Oct 10, 2025; 2,400+ violations documented — 857+ Palestinians killed since ceasefire as of May 17, 2026 (ACLED: April 2026 deadliest month of year, 140 fatalities). Hamas has no named military successor to al-Haddad. UN Security Council open debate: Deputy Special Coordinator calls for ceasefire consolidation and halt to Israeli violations. May 16 (Day 952): IDF confirms killing of Izz al-Din al-Haddad — Hamas military wing head, 'last architect of October 7,' personal captor of 5 Nahal Oz surveillance soldiers; killed in Gaza City Rimal airstrike. May 15 (Day 951): JPPI poll — 63% of Israelis support immediate October 7 commission; 47 days to July 1 Supreme Court investigation deadline. May 13 (Day 949): Knesset committee reveals Likud inquiry bill stripped 'full, thorough, independent' language; October Council declares 'political whitewash.' May 12 (Day 948): Civil Commission final report — October 7 sexual violence systematic, widespread, deliberate strategy; new findings on sexual abuse of minors; Knesset passes 93-0 military tribunal law for ~300 October 7 perpetrators. ICC arrest warrants for Netanyahu and Gallant remain active. Gaza reconstruction cost: $71.4B per UN-EU-World Bank joint assessment; <$1B of $17B pledged received.
